title: cadintent core geometry
description: Core geometry primitives: point, polyline (straight + bulge-arc segments), arc, circle — all in flat (x, y) plan coordinates. The model is 2.5D: elevations are typed quantities on objects, never a third coordinate. Spec version 0.1.0.

Point.description: A position in project-local flat plan coordinates. Values are coordinate-quantum decimal strings in SI metres.

PolylineVertex.description: One polyline vertex. 'bulge' = tan(sweep/4) of the circular-arc segment from this vertex to the next (positive = counter-clockwise); omitted or '0' means a straight segment. Ratio-quantum decimal string.

PolylineGeometry.description: An open or closed polyline of straight and bulge-arc segments. When closed, the segment from the last vertex back to the first (with the last vertex's bulge) closes the figure, and the polyline doubles as a region.

ArcGeometry.description: A circular arc from 'start' to 'end' with 'bulge' = tan(sweep/4), non-zero (kernel-enforced), positive = counter-clockwise.

Geometry.description: One core geometry primitive. Ellipses and splines are not core; they enter as tessellated arc-polylines with the original recorded as evidence.

Region.description: A closed polyline used as a region (e.g. a scope declaration's plan region).

ElevationKind.description: The two elevation kinds — never interchangeable.

Elevation.description: A typed elevation quantity attached to an object — never a third coordinate on a point. Value is an elevation-quantum decimal string in SI metres; every elevation carries its kind and its sources.

sources.description: Where this elevation came from: typed citations (evidence for surveyed shots, commands for interpolations, statements for asserted values).

UnitSystemDeclaration.description: A project's unit system: metric, or imperial with an explicit foot choice. Stored values are always SI metres; the unit system governs which quanta apply and how values are formatted at every boundary.

ImperialUnitSystem.description: Imperial units with an explicit, mandatory foot choice: international foot (0.3048 m exact) is the conventional default; US survey foot (1200/3937 m) only by deliberate opt-in.

CrsDeclaration.description: Optional metadata naming the real-world coordinate reference system the project's local plane corresponds to. Metadata only — the kernel never transforms coordinates.

description.description: Optional human-readable description, e.g. 'NAD83 / UTM zone 10N'.
